items.title: Emmanuel Sayles Interview, 1961-01-29
items.q: I mean, I was working with bands like Sidney and Poulon

ctx.x: You weren't with the WPA at all, wasn't he?

No, I didn't go because I could always do better without the WPA. I mean, I was working with bands like Sidney and Poulon, and I had other guys I'd be working with when, uh, the big band wouldn't be working, you know? But, like, this time of year, say, from the holiday, Christmas holidays, and to Mardi Gras, man, we'd be busy. Yeah. Only time we'd have a break was after, uh, Mardi Gras, between Mardi Gras and during the Lent, see? Mm-hmm. And those days.
And, uh, you were just, like, gigging around now, you know? I mean, you were just freelancing now?

items.title: Emmanuel Sayles Interview, 1979-12-05
items.q: After work with Sidney Desvene, I worked with the Redford Band and went with the Pudon Band. I was working with the Pudon Band here. He used to play at the Country Club

ctx.x: How long did you stay in Pensacola?

Oh, I think it was, let's see, I went there in 24, I must have came around about, no, about 20 years, about three years, about 27 years. I said, well, when the job was closed and we left Pensacola, and one stayed in Mobile, and they had a union there. They had a union in Jacksonville. We didn't have no union, black union in New Orleans. And when I was coming back, I told my daddy, this thing was really getting bad.
